title: The Big House, the log cabin, the move to Durham and his mother's schooling
summary: He recalls the family homes in Red Springs, his siblings, the move to Durham and his mother teaching him to read and count before school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Back in Red Springs, North Carolina, as I first remember, we lived in my grandmother's house, which we always called The Big House. Later on, my brothers and my father and his brothers, my uncles, they built a small little house themselves out about a half-a-mile away from my grandmother's house. I guess you would call it a log cabin of some sort, because they split the rails and built it themselves. My parents stayed there until after my sister was born, which was the third child. I had a brother that was next to me, and then my oldest sister, whose name was Marian, was the third. I guess I was about a little over 4 years old then.

The family decided to move to Durham, North Carolina, which is where I started elementary school. I guess when you're that age, around 4 or 5, you really begin to really become aware of your surroundings and going to school and whatever. My mother is the kind of person that always had a thirst for education. She didn't have very much herself. I think she went to about the Eighth Grade, which back during those times for a Black person was a pretty high education to have. If I remember, my father went through about the Third or Fourth Grade.

But anyway, my mother always had this thing for music and education of any kind. As a matter of fact, she taught me to... When I went to elementary school I was 6 years old, and by the time I went to elementary school she had taught me to read and write and add and subtract. So when I got to elementary school, I was a little bit ahead of the game. I guess I had the kindergarten training at home, which I don't remember them even having a kindergarten in school then.
